name: Bento Grid Slider
summary: An asymmetric grid of rounded tiles at mixed sizes — one dominant hero tile, a solid copy/CTA panel, a rhythm of smaller category cells — where the grid skeleton is the slide frame: advancing swaps every tile's content in place while the layout never moves, marrying dashboard density with slideshow storytelling.

composition: Asymmetric bento balance: a dominant photo hero tile paired with a solid-color text/CTA tile of similar visual mass, then smaller equal category tiles — never a uniform grid.
Consistent rounded corners and tight UNIFORM gutters are what make it read as 'bento'; one wrong gutter breaks the box.
Labeled photo tiles double as content preview AND navigation entry points into sub-topics.
Type steps from a big name in the hero tile to small eyebrow labels in the cells — the grid provides the hierarchy, so type stays quiet.
layering: Essentially flat single-plane tiling; depth is subtle tile elevation (soft shadow/inset) and the photo-vs-solid-plate contrast, not parallax.
Solid text plates set AMONG photo plates give the eye resting points inside the density.
lighting: Flat even UI lighting with gentle tile shadows for separation; drama lives INSIDE the photos, never in the chrome.
The grid must stay calm so any photo set drops in — lighting effects on tiles fight the modular logic.
typography: Large humanist display for the featured name; lowercase category labels; guidebook-like quiet legibility.
Weight contrast between the big place/product name and small tile eyebrows carries the hierarchy.

rules: One warm/neutral tile-chrome system (e.g. a two-tone neutral pair) unifies the grid so any content set's photos read as curated.
Accent restraint keeps the bento calm — a single UI accent at most, spent outside the photographic tiles.
Photo tiles must share a tonal register (same grade family) or the grid fragments.

easing: Soft ease-in-out crossfades of tile CONTENTS in place — the grid geometry holds perfectly still.
Slight cell-to-cell stagger on the swap so the board visibly ripples to the new state.
pacing: Calm mid-tempo state changes (~1s), browsable rather than kinetic.
Hover states on tiles may lift/zoom the photo INSIDE its frame; the frame itself never moves.
choreography: The fixed skeleton is the stage; on advance, tiles crossfade their photos and labels in a light stagger so the whole board morphs to a new subject without layout jumps.
Never re-flow the grid on advance — layout constancy is the family's identity.

gapNotes: Rounded-tile plane composition with in-place texture crossfade is expressible node-by-node, but there is no bento LAYOUT primitive (grid solver with mixed spans + uniform gutters) — Conductor would have to hand-place every tile.
The coordinated all-tiles content swap needs the same multi-node state driver as infinite-filmstrip-gallery's theme swap.
True flat/orthographic composition belongs to the W-2D hub mode; in 3D perspective today, tile grids show slight keystoning at frame edges.

whenToUse: Overview/comparison surfaces: travel destinations, product ranges, feature matrices, dashboards with editorial ambition.
When the brief wants density AND premium calm — bento is the highest-information premium pattern in the corpus.
SaaS marketing where feature tiles double as navigation.
whenNotToUse: Single-focus linear narratives — the grid fragments attention across many tiles by design.
When tile imagery varies wildly in tone and breaks the unified set.
Tiny viewports: bento collapses to a column and loses its identity; needs a designed mobile fallback.

notes: Bento is the anti-spectacle family: it pairs with calm editorial registers and clashes with every full-frame motion family.
Category tiles can deep-link into hubs rendered by other families — bento as the map, immersive families as the territory.

antiRepetition.notes: Counts as a carousel mechanic (the grid IS the slide frame) — same cluster as filmstrip-3d-carousel, coverflow-3d-carousel, swatch-variant-swap.

sources.title: Bento Grid Travel Slider
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: prev/next driven through multiple destinations; in-place tile content crossfade with the grid skeleton perfectly static observed across advances; tile hover states checked.

exemplars.promptSummary: Mixed-size rounded tiles with uniform gutters on a warm off-white canvas — a large travel-photo feature tile beside a soft 3D gradient orb, a muted map, and a stat card — the bento layout language as a still.
exemplars.notes: ORIGINAL render (Replicate black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro, ~$0.06). Subject deliberately distinct from any analyzed source template. Illustrates the family aesthetic target (palette/composition/lighting); does NOT demonstrate runtime motion or in-engine execution.
